questions.q: What is the risk-neutral probability, p, used for in the binomial model?
options: It is the trader's actual forecast of the probability the stock goes up
It is a pricing device chosen so that the stock's expected return under p equals the risk-free rate, enabling arbitrage-free discounting
It is always exactly 0.5 regardless of volatility
It represents the probability the option expires in the money
questions.explain: Risk-neutral probability is not a real-world forecast. It's constructed so discounting expected payoffs under it at the risk-free rate produces an arbitrage-free price.

questions.q: In backward induction, how is an option's value at an earlier node computed from its two successor nodes?
options: By averaging V_up and V_down with no discounting
By taking the maximum of V_up and V_down
By adding V_up and V_down together
questions.explain: The node value is the risk-neutral expected value of its two successors, discounted back one step at the risk-free rate.

questions.q: Why does the binomial model handle American options more naturally than a closed-form formula like Black-Scholes?
options: American options cannot be priced at all
Because at each node, the model can compare the value of holding against the value of immediate exercise and take the larger, which a single closed-form equation cannot do
Because American options have no strike price
Because the binomial model ignores volatility
questions.explain: The step-by-step tree structure lets you check the early-exercise decision at every single node, which is exactly what American-style exercise rights require.

questions.q: What happens to the binomial model's price as the number of time steps N increases (with step size shrinking accordingly)?
options: It stays exactly the same regardless of N
It converges to the Black-Scholes price for the equivalent European option
It converges to the stock's current spot price
questions.explain: The binomial model is a discrete-time approximation of the same no-arbitrage logic Black-Scholes applies in continuous time, so as N grows, the two converge.
